title: German A2 Everyday Vocabulary — Unique Compared with A1

comparison_basis.a2_source: German A2 Vocabulary for Everyday Life in Germany
comparison_basis.method: Compared normalized German headwords (ignoring noun articles and dictionary plural suffixes). Removed A2 entries already listed in A1 and repeated A2 headwords. Similar English meanings are not automatically treated as duplicates.
comparison_basis.important_note: This is a practical lexical comparison, not a claim that every word is officially exclusive to CEFR A2. Expressions containing familiar A1 words are kept when they add a distinct everyday meaning.

synonym_groups.meaning: to postpone / move to a later time
synonym_groups.note: verschieben is the most common everyday choice.

synonym_groups.meaning: to cancel an appointment or plan
synonym_groups.note: stornieren is especially common for bookings, orders, and reservations.
abholen is used for a person, parcel, or order; einsammeln often means collect several things or people.
in Ordnung bringen is an everyday expression; context determines the best choice.
dürfen is a modal verb; erlaubt sein is an adjective phrase.
Usually interchangeable in everyday sentences.
anschließend is a little more formal.
Usually interchangeable with numbers and amounts.
Not exact synonyms: sich freuen describes feeling glad or looking forward to something; glücklich sein means to be happy.

synonym_groups.meaning: to tell someone / let someone know
synonym_groups.note: Bescheid sagen is conversational; informieren is more formal.
Both can mean submit, but abgeben is also used for handing something over.
Verspätung haben is common for trains/buses; sich verspäten is common for people too.
aufräumen is the natural everyday verb.

synonym_groups.meaning: to be reachable / available by phone
synonym_groups.note: Related meanings, not perfectly interchangeable.
begreifen can imply understanding something more fully.
nett means nice; freundlich specifically means friendly.
wunderschön is stronger: very beautiful.
günstig often sounds more positive; billig can sometimes suggest low quality.
bestellen is the normal choice in restaurants and shops; ordern is more limited.
Not exact synonyms: absagen means someone cancels; ausfallen means an event/service does not take place.
